title: A Regime-Activated Lensing Response Improves the Fit to KiDS-1000 Cosmic Shear and Reframes the Interpretation of S8
description: Tests a phenomenological, regime-activated lensing response Σ(k,z) that modifies how matter fluctuations source shear, applied to KiDS-1000 cosmic shear. Finds a large maximum-likelihood improvement over ΛCDM at fixed cosmology that cannot be mimicked by a simple amplitude rescaling, with a distinct low-redshift tomographic signature that reframes the S8 tension as a response effect.

S8_definition.description: Standard cosmic shear amplitude compression used in ΛCDM analyses.

Effective_power.description: Phenomenological modification of the lensing power via a scale- and redshift-dependent response Σ(k,z).

Sigma_factor.description: Regime-activated response: smooth transition in k around k_trans and a late-time activation below z_activ; defaults to unity outside the active regime.

Reframed_shear_amplitude.description: Decomposition of the observed shear amplitude into growth (σ8) and lensing response (Σ) factors at a representative pivot.

key_results.main_finding: Including a late-time, small-scale lensing response Σ(k,z) improves the KiDS-1000 cosmic shear likelihood by Δ(−2 ln L) ≈ −50.9 at fixed Planck-2018 cosmology, with a distinct low-z tomographic signature and robustness to scale cuts, and cannot be replicated by simple amplitude rescaling.
datasets_used: KiDS-1000 cosmic shear ξ± (Asgari et al. 2021) with public covariance and n(z)

sealed_predictions.statement: Across independent weak-lensing surveys (e.g., DES-Y3, HSC), freeing a Σ(k,z) of the same functional form will yield a concentrated likelihood improvement in low-z tomographic bins (z ≲ 0.5) with negligible preference at high z (z ≳ 0.7).
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Reanalysis of DES-Y3/HSC tomographic ξ± showing no low-z–localized improvement and a best-fit α consistent with zero within ±0.02.

sealed_predictions.statement: CMB lensing × galaxy lensing cross-correlations at effective z ≳ 0.7 will prefer Σ ≈ 1, while galaxy lensing auto/cross at z ≈ 0.2–0.5 and k ≳ 0.1 h Mpc−1 will prefer Σ > 1 by O(10%).
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Joint analysis of CMB lensing (Planck/ACT/SPT) with low-z shear that constrains Σ to unity at both low and high redshift with ≤5% precision at k ≳ 0.1 h Mpc−1.

kill_criteria: KC1: Full posterior analyses (with standard WL nuisance marginalization: IA, m-calibration, photo-z, baryons) show no preference for Σ (best-fit α → 0 with |α| < 0.02 at 95% CL) and negligible model selection support (evidence ΔlnZ ≤ 1) in KiDS-1000.

KC2: Cross-survey replication (DES-Y3, HSC, KiDS) with a common pipeline finds that allowing Σ(k,z) yields no low-z–localized improvement and total Δ(−2 ln L) improvement < 10 over ΛCDM amplitude changes alone.
KC3: Tomographic split tests contradict the predicted fingerprint, with high-z bins (z ≳ 0.7) showing equal or larger preference for Σ > 1 than low-z bins.
KC4: CMB lensing auto and CMB lensing × galaxy lensing jointly constrain the response at 0.1 ≲ k/(h Mpc−1) ≲ 0.3 and 0.2 ≲ z ≲ 0.5 to Σ = 1.00 ± 0.05, excluding the inferred Σ ≈ 1.13 pivot response.

KC5: Shear-ratio and E/B-mode null tests within KiDS-1000 limit any scale- or redshift-dependent lensing response to <3% across the model’s active regime, inconsistent with the required O(10%) response.
KC6: The observed improvement is fully absorbed by physically motivated baryonic feedback and/or intrinsic alignment models under standard priors, eliminating the need for Σ(k,z).

paper.title: A Regime-Activated Lensing Response Improves the Fit to KiDS-1000 Cosmic Shear and Reframes the S8 Tension

abstract.problem: KiDS-1000 and other weak lensing surveys measure S8 values 2-3σ below Planck-CMB predictions
abstract.method: Introduce regime-activated lensing response Σ(k,z) that modifies matter-light coupling
abstract.result: Likelihood improvement Δ(-2lnL) ≈ -50.9, S8 tension effectively resolved
abstract.interpretation: Tension reframed as lensing coupling difference, not σ8 discrepancy

redshift_dependence.formula_active: Σ_z(z) = 1 + α × (1 - z/z_activ) for z < z_activ

reframing.interpretation: Tension dissolves when lensing response is accounted for

physical_motivation.mechanism: Entropy gradients modify metric perturbation coupling matter to light
physical_motivation.relation_to_galaxy_scales: Σ(k,z) is cosmological analog of μ(g_bar) at galaxy scales
